skill.name: write-app-change-log
skill.description: Generates and updates the latest Android app changelog from git history since the most recent version tag.
skill.summary: Creates concise app release notes from recent git commits and existing changelog style.

content.value_statement: Release notes are hard to keep concise and consistent across Android releases. This skill reviews git history and existing changelog style to draft a user-focused update.
actual_capabilities: Fetches or reviews git tags to identify the latest version baseline.
Collects commit titles and descriptions from the latest tag to HEAD.
Filters commits for user-facing app changes and bug fixes.
Matches the tone and format of existing fastlane changelog files.
Updates the highest numbered Android changelog file with concise release text.
limitations: Requires access to a git repository with version tags and commit history.
Depends on clear commit messages to identify meaningful user-facing changes.
Targets the existing fastlane Android changelog layout used by the project.
Does not verify release readiness beyond changelog content and version metadata.

use_cases.title: Prepare Android Release Notes
use_cases.description: Create a concise changelog entry before publishing a new Android app build.

use_cases.title: Summarize User-Facing Changes
use_cases.description: Turn recent commits into clear release text that avoids internal implementation details.

use_cases.title: Maintain Changelog Consistency
use_cases.description: Match the wording, structure, and length of previous fastlane changelog entries.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard release note update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the write-app-change-log skill to draft the latest Android changelog from recent git history.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on User Value
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that emphasizes app-facing improvements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the write-app-change-log skill. Include only changes that affect app users, and exclude CI, build, and internal documentation work.

prompt_templates.title: Match Existing Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for consistency with previous releases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the write-app-change-log skill. Read the recent fastlane changelog entries first, then update the latest file in the same tone and format.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before a release branch is finalized.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the write-app-change-log skill. Compare commits since the latest v* tag, pick key user-facing changes, verify version metadata, and update the latest changelog file.

output_examples.input: Generate the changelog for the current Android release.
output_examples.output: A concise fastlane changelog entry that names the release and lists the most important user-facing fixes or improvements.

output_examples.input: Update the latest changelog, but ignore infrastructure and CI commits.
output_examples.output: A revised changelog file focused on app behavior, interface changes, performance improvements, and visible bug fixes.

output_examples.input: Match the previous changelog style for this project.
output_examples.output: Release text that follows the existing wording, bullet style, and level of detail used by recent changelog entries.

best_practices: Review the selected commits before publishing the final changelog.
Keep entries short and focused on changes users can notice.
Confirm the version name and version code before release packaging.
anti_patterns: Including CI, dependency, or build-system changes that users cannot observe.
Copying raw commit messages directly into public release notes.
Publishing a changelog without checking the existing project style.

faq.question: What does this skill update?
faq.answer: It updates the highest numbered Android changelog file under the project fastlane metadata path.

faq.question: Does it include every commit?
faq.answer: No. It selects the most meaningful user-facing changes and excludes most infrastructure and maintenance commits.

faq.question: Does it need git tags?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow uses the latest version tag as the baseline for collecting release commits.

faq.question: Can it write app store text?
faq.answer: Yes. It drafts concise release-note text suitable for Android fastlane changelog files.

faq.question: Does it decide the release version?
faq.answer: No. It checks the current version metadata, but the project release process remains authoritative.

faq.question: Is it limited to AnySoftKeyboard?
faq.answer: It is tailored to this repository layout, but the workflow can inform similar Android projects using fastlane changelogs.
